---------------------------- MODULE W4Od2m9p3t2 ----------------------------
(* Warehouse robot fleet: two independent fleets (A and B) share one pool of
   docking slots. Allocations are stamped with an epoch number; a
   reconfiguration bumps the epoch and clears every allocation.  Safety: the
   same slot is never simultaneously granted to two different robots. *)
EXTENDS Naturals

Slots    == {"s1", "s2"}
FleetA   == {"a1"}
FleetB   == {"b1"}
Robots   == FleetA \cup FleetB
MaxEpoch == 2

VARIABLES grants, epoch

Grant(s, r) == [slot |-> s, robot |-> r]

TypeOK ==
    /\ grants \subseteq [slot: Slots, robot: Robots]
    /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch

Init ==
    /\ grants = {}
    /\ epoch = 0

SlotFree(s) == \A g \in grants : g.slot # s

Claim(r, s) ==
    /\ SlotFree(s)
    /\ grants' = grants \cup {Grant(s, r)}
    /\ epoch' = epoch

Release(r, s) ==
    /\ Grant(s, r) \in grants
    /\ grants' = grants \ {Grant(s, r)}
    /\ epoch' = epoch

Reconfigure ==
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ grants' = {}

Next ==
    \E r \in Robots, s \in Slots :
        \/ Claim(r, s)
        \/ Release(r, s)
        \/ Reconfigure

NoDoubleAllocation ==
    \A g1, g2 \in grants :
        (g1.slot = g2.slot) => (g1.robot = g2.robot)

vars == <<grants, epoch>>
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoDoubleAllocation
nl:
In a warehouse, two independent robot fleets, fleet A and fleet B, share a single pool of docking slots. Each fleet dispatches robots that must claim a slot before recharging, and because the two fleets are operated separately they draw from the same physical pool without a shared coordinator. Every allocation is stamped with the current epoch number so operators can tell which reconfiguration cycle it belongs to. Periodically the warehouse controller performs an epoch-numbered reconfiguration: it increments the epoch and clears all outstanding slot allocations so the layout can be recomputed. A robot may claim a slot only when that slot currently holds no allocation, and it may later release a slot it holds. The hazard is that, with two fleets pulling from one pool, the same slot could be handed to a robot from fleet A and a robot from fleet B at the same time. The model tracks the set of active grants and the epoch counter.
SAFETY PROPERTY: No docking slot is ever allocated to two different robots at the same time.

spec_text:
-------------------------- MODULE W4Od7m1p6t1 --------------------------
(* Container-ship crane yard.  Cranes sit on a token ring; only the crane
   currently holding the token may operate a container move.  The token is
   passed by grant messages that can be delivered out of order, so a stale
   grant (carrying an old version) must never re-authorize a crane.  Each
   grant carries the token version it was minted at; a delivery only takes
   effect when its version matches the current version. *)
EXTENDS Naturals

Cranes  == {"c1", "c2", "c3"}
MaxVer  == 3
NoOne   == "none"

VARIABLES holder, curVer, inflight, operator

TypeInv ==
    /\ holder \in Cranes \cup {NoOne}
    /\ curVer \in 1..MaxVer
    /\ operator \in Cranes \cup {NoOne}
    /\ inflight \subseteq [to : Cranes, ver : 1..MaxVer]

Init ==
    /\ holder = "c1"
    /\ curVer = 1
    /\ inflight = {}
    /\ operator = NoOne

Grant(c) ==
    /\ holder # NoOne
    /\ operator = NoOne
    /\ curVer < MaxVer
    /\ curVer' = curVer + 1
    /\ inflight' = inflight \union {[to |-> c, ver |-> curVer + 1]}
    /\ holder' = NoOne
    /\ operator' = operator

Deliver(g) ==
    /\ g \in inflight
    /\ inflight' = inflight \ {g}
    /\ holder' = IF g.ver = curVer THEN g.to ELSE holder
    /\ UNCHANGED <<curVer, operator>>

Operate(c) ==
    /\ holder = c
    /\ operator = NoOne
    /\ operator' = c
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, curVer, inflight>>

Finish ==
    /\ operator # NoOne
    /\ operator' = NoOne
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, curVer, inflight>>

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Cranes : Grant(c)
    \/ \E g \in inflight : Deliver(g)
    \/ \E c \in Cranes : Operate(c)
    \/ Finish

OnlyCurrentHolderOperates ==
    (operator # NoOne) => (operator = holder)

vars == <<holder, curVer, inflight, operator>>
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
=======================================================================

INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT OnlyCurrentHolderOperates
nl:
In a container-ship crane yard, three cranes are arranged on a token ring and only the crane holding the token is allowed to perform a container move. When the token holder wants to pass control onward it mints a grant message stamped with the new token version and sends it around the ring. Because the network reorders messages, several grants may be in flight at once and can arrive in any order, so a crane might receive an old grant after a newer one. To prevent a stale grant from re-authorizing a crane, each delivery only takes effect when the grant's version matches the current token version; grants carrying an out-of-date version are dropped on arrival. A crane may begin operating only while it actually holds the token, and it finishes before the token moves on. The model tracks the current holder, the current version, the set of in-flight grants, and which crane is operating.
SAFETY PROPERTY: A crane is never operating unless it is the current holder of the token.

-------------------------- MODULE W4Od2m2p0t1 --------------------------
(* Warehouse robot fleet coordinating access to one critical resource (a
   single charging bay) with a two-phase-commit-style handshake: a robot
   announces intent (phase 1), the coordinator commits the bay to exactly one
   requester and emits a grant, and the robot enters only when it receives
   that grant.  Grant messages travel on a reordering network, so they sit in
   an in-flight set and may be delivered in any order.  Safety: no two robots
   occupy the charging bay simultaneously. *)
EXTENDS Naturals

Robots == {"p1", "p2"}
NoOne  == "none"

VARIABLES intent, owner, cs, grants

TypeInv ==
    /\ intent \subseteq Robots
    /\ owner \in Robots \cup {NoOne}
    /\ cs \subseteq Robots
    /\ grants \subseteq [to : Robots]

Init ==
    /\ intent = {}
    /\ owner = NoOne
    /\ cs = {}
    /\ grants = {}

Request(p) ==
    /\ p \notin intent
    /\ intent' = intent \union {p}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, cs, grants>>

Commit(p) ==
    /\ owner = NoOne
    /\ p \in intent
    /\ owner' = p
    /\ grants' = grants \union {[to |-> p]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<intent, cs>>

Enter(p) ==
    /\ [to |-> p] \in grants
    /\ cs' = cs \union {p}
    /\ grants' = grants \ {[to |-> p]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<intent, owner>>

Leave(p) ==
    /\ p \in cs
    /\ cs' = cs \ {p}
    /\ owner' = NoOne
    /\ intent' = intent \ {p}
    /\ UNCHANGED grants

Next ==
    \E p \in Robots :
        \/ Request(p)
        \/ Commit(p)
        \/ Enter(p)
        \/ Leave(p)

MutualExclusion == \A a, b \in cs : a = b

vars == <<intent, owner, cs, grants>>
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
=======================================================================
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT MutualExclusion
nl:
In a warehouse robot fleet, robots must take turns using a single charging bay, which is the critical resource. Access is arbitrated with a two-phase-commit-style handshake across the participants: in the first phase a robot announces its intent to charge, and in the second phase the coordinator commits the bay to exactly one requester and issues a grant. A robot may physically enter the bay only once it has received its grant. Grants travel over a network that can reorder messages, so at any moment several grants may be sitting in an in-flight pool and may be delivered in any order. When a robot finishes charging it leaves the bay and releases ownership so the coordinator can commit the bay to someone else. The model tracks the set of robots that have announced intent, the current owner, the set of robots inside the bay, and the pool of in-flight grants.
SAFETY PROPERTY: At no point do two different robots occupy the charging bay at the same time.

spec_text:
-------------------------- MODULE W4Od3m6p5t3 --------------------------
(* Bank interbank settlement batch.  A settlement processor must hold a valid,
   time-limited lease to settle the batch, and settling is irreversible.  A
   lease has an expiry time; once the clock passes the expiry the lease is
   dead and another processor may acquire a fresh one.  A processor can be
   slow (its own clock advances) but does not fail, so a laggard may try to
   settle after its lease has already expired -- which must be rejected.
   Safety: the irreversible settlement happens at most once. *)
EXTENDS Naturals

Banks    == {"bankA", "bankB"}
NoOne    == "none"
MaxClock == 3
Lease    == 2

VARIABLES clock, leaseOwner, leaseExpiry, settleCount

TypeInv ==
    /\ clock \in 0..MaxClock
    /\ leaseOwner \in Banks \cup {NoOne}
    /\ leaseExpiry \in 0..(MaxClock + Lease)
    /\ settleCount \in 0..2

Init ==
    /\ clock = 0
    /\ leaseOwner = NoOne
    /\ leaseExpiry = 0
    /\ settleCount = 0

Tick ==
    /\ clock < MaxClock
    /\ clock' = clock + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leaseOwner, leaseExpiry, settleCount>>

Acquire(b) ==
    /\ (leaseOwner = NoOne) \/ (clock >= leaseExpiry)
    /\ leaseOwner' = b
    /\ leaseExpiry' = clock + Lease
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, settleCount>>

Settle(b) ==
    /\ leaseOwner = b
    /\ clock < leaseExpiry
    /\ settleCount = 0
    /\ settleCount' = settleCount + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, leaseOwner, leaseExpiry>>

Release ==
    /\ leaseOwner # NoOne
    /\ leaseOwner' = NoOne
    /\ leaseExpiry' = 0
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, settleCount>>

Next ==
    \/ Tick
    \/ \E b \in Banks : Acquire(b)
    \/ \E b \in Banks : Settle(b)
    \/ Release

SettleAtMostOnce == settleCount <= 1

vars == <<clock, leaseOwner, leaseExpiry, settleCount>>
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
=======================================================================
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT SettleAtMostOnce
nl:
A bank's interbank settlement batch must be settled exactly once, and settling is an irreversible action that moves real money. To coordinate which processor settles, the system uses lease-based ownership with an expiry: a processor acquires a lease stamped with an expiry time, and the lease is only valid while the clock has not yet reached that expiry. Once a lease expires, any processor may acquire a fresh lease. A processor may be slow, meaning its local clock advances and it can lag behind, but it does not crash; the danger is that a slow processor tries to settle using a lease that has already expired. To guard against this, a processor may settle only while it currently holds the lease and the clock has not passed the expiry, and only if the batch has not already been settled. The model tracks the clock, the current lease owner, the lease expiry time, and how many times settlement has occurred.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The irreversible settlement of the batch occurs at most once.

spec_text:
------------------------- MODULE W4Od13m2p5t1 -------------------------
(* Vending-machine network settling a purchase with two-phase commit.  The
   participant machines vote to commit; when all have voted yes the
   coordinator decides commit and broadcasts commit acknowledgements.  The
   physical dispense of the product is the irreversible action and must happen
   at most once.  Acknowledgements ride a reordering network (an in-flight
   set delivered in any order), so a reordered or duplicated commit ack must
   not cause a second dispense. *)
EXTENDS Naturals

Machines == {"m1", "m2"}
NoOne    == "none"

VARIABLES yesSet, decided, acks, dispensed

TypeInv ==
    /\ yesSet \subseteq Machines
    /\ decided \in {"none", "commit"}
    /\ acks \subseteq [to : Machines]
    /\ dispensed \in 0..2

Init ==
    /\ yesSet = {}
    /\ decided = "none"
    /\ acks = {}
    /\ dispensed = 0

Vote(p) ==
    /\ p \notin yesSet
    /\ yesSet' = yesSet \union {p}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<decided, acks, dispensed>>

Decide ==
    /\ decided = "none"
    /\ yesSet = Machines
    /\ decided' = "commit"
    /\ acks' = {[to |-> p] : p \in Machines}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<yesSet, dispensed>>

DeliverDispense(p) ==
    /\ [to |-> p] \in acks
    /\ dispensed = 0
    /\ dispensed' = 1
    /\ acks' = acks \ {[to |-> p]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<yesSet, decided>>

DropAck(p) ==
    /\ [to |-> p] \in acks
    /\ dispensed = 1
    /\ acks' = acks \ {[to |-> p]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<yesSet, decided, dispensed>>

Reset ==
    /\ decided = "commit"
    /\ acks = {}
    /\ yesSet' = {}
    /\ decided' = "none"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<acks, dispensed>>

Next ==
    \/ \E p \in Machines : Vote(p)
    \/ Decide
    \/ \E p \in Machines : DeliverDispense(p)
    \/ \E p \in Machines : DropAck(p)
    \/ Reset

DispenseAtMostOnce == dispensed <= 1

vars == <<yesSet, decided, acks, dispensed>>
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
=======================================================================
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT DispenseAtMostOnce
nl:
A network of vending machines settles a purchase using two-phase commit across the participant machines. In the voting phase each machine casts a yes vote, and once every participant has voted yes the coordinator decides to commit and broadcasts commit acknowledgements to the machines. The irreversible action is the physical dispensing of the product, which must happen at most once for the transaction. The commit acknowledgements travel over a network that can reorder and duplicate messages, so they are held in an in-flight pool and delivered in any order. When an acknowledgement is delivered the product is dispensed, but only if it has not already been dispensed; leftover or reordered acknowledgements arriving afterward are simply discarded. The model tracks the set of yes votes, the coordinator's decision, the pool of in-flight acknowledgements, and how many times the product has been dispensed.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The product is physically dispensed at most once per committed transaction.

spec_text:
------------------------- MODULE W4Od17m0p4t4 -------------------------
(* Airport baggage router feeding one chute that has a bounded capacity.
   Handlers add bags using optimistic locking with retry: each add first
   snapshots the current load, and only commits if the load is still the
   snapshotted value (compare-and-set); otherwise it retries with a fresh
   snapshot.  The chute capacity can change at runtime (a chute may be
   resized), but never below the current load.  Safety: the number of bags on
   the chute never exceeds its capacity. *)
EXTENDS Naturals

MaxCap == 3

VARIABLES load, capacity, inflight

TypeInv ==
    /\ load \in 0..MaxCap
    /\ capacity \in 1..MaxCap
    /\ inflight \subseteq [expect : 0..MaxCap]

Init ==
    /\ load = 0
    /\ capacity = 2
    /\ inflight = {}

BeginAdd ==
    /\ inflight' = inflight \union {[expect |-> load]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<load, capacity>>

CommitAdd(r) ==
    /\ r \in inflight
    /\ r.expect = load
    /\ load < capacity
    /\ load' = load + 1
    /\ inflight' = inflight \ {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED capacity

RetryAdd(r) ==
    /\ r \in inflight
    /\ r.expect # load
    /\ inflight' = (inflight \ {r}) \union {[expect |-> load]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<load, capacity>>

RejectAdd(r) ==
    /\ r \in inflight
    /\ r.expect = load
    /\ load >= capacity
    /\ inflight' = inflight \ {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<load, capacity>>

RemoveBag ==
    /\ load > 0
    /\ load' = load - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<capacity, inflight>>

Resize ==
    /\ \E c \in 1..MaxCap :
        /\ c >= load
        /\ capacity' = c
    /\ UNCHANGED <<load, inflight>>

Next ==
    \/ BeginAdd
    \/ \E r \in inflight : CommitAdd(r)
    \/ \E r \in inflight : RetryAdd(r)
    \/ \E r \in inflight : RejectAdd(r)
    \/ RemoveBag
    \/ Resize

WithinCapacity == load <= capacity

vars == <<load, capacity, inflight>>
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
=======================================================================
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT WithinCapacity
nl:
An airport baggage router feeds bags onto a single chute that has a bounded capacity. Handlers add bags concurrently using optimistic locking with retry: before committing an add, a handler takes a snapshot of the current load, and it only completes the add if the load is still exactly what it snapshotted, which is a compare-and-set. If some other handler changed the load in the meantime, the add fails its check and retries with a fresh snapshot. An add that finds the chute already full is rejected instead of committed. The chute's capacity can be changed at runtime when the chute is resized, but it is never lowered below the number of bags currently on it. Bags also leave the chute over time, lowering the load. The model tracks the current load, the current capacity, and the set of in-flight optimistic add attempts with their snapshots.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of bags on the chute never exceeds its current capacity.

spec_text:
------------------------- MODULE W4Od18m5p6t5 -------------------------
(* Smart-home door-lock network.  Each sensitive action (unlocking a door)
   requires a quorum of participant devices to vote for it in the CURRENT
   round.  Configuration rounds advance over time; a vote cast in an older
   round is stale and must not count toward the quorum.  A privileged admin
   may override and authorize an action without a quorum.  Every execution
   records how many valid (current-round) votes backed it and whether the
   admin override was in force.  Safety: no action executes unless it was
   authorized -- either by a genuine current-round quorum or by the admin. *)
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

Devices  == {"d1", "d2", "d3"}
Quorum   == 2
MaxRound == 2

VARIABLES round, votes, override, execLog

TypeInv ==
    /\ round \in 0..MaxRound
    /\ votes \subseteq [who : Devices, rnd : 0..MaxRound]
    /\ override \in BOOLEAN
    /\ execLog \subseteq [nvotes : 0..3, ovr : BOOLEAN]

Init ==
    /\ round = 0
    /\ votes = {}
    /\ override = FALSE
    /\ execLog = {}

ValidVotes == { v \in votes : v.rnd = round }

Vote(d) ==
    /\ [who |-> d, rnd |-> round] \notin votes
    /\ votes' = votes \union {[who |-> d, rnd |-> round]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<round, override, execLog>>

AdminOverride ==
    /\ override' = TRUE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<round, votes, execLog>>

Reconfigure ==
    /\ round < MaxRound
    /\ round' = round + 1
    /\ override' = FALSE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, execLog>>

Execute ==
    /\ (Cardinality(ValidVotes) >= Quorum) \/ override
    /\ execLog' = execLog \union
                    {[nvotes |-> Cardinality(ValidVotes), ovr |-> override]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<round, votes, override>>

Next ==
    \/ \E d \in Devices : Vote(d)
    \/ AdminOverride
    \/ Reconfigure
    \/ Execute

AuthorizedExecutionsOnly ==
    \A e \in execLog : (e.nvotes >= Quorum) \/ e.ovr

vars == <<round, votes, override, execLog>>
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
=======================================================================
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT AuthorizedExecutionsOnly
nl:
In a smart-home door-lock network, unlocking a door is a sensitive action that requires a quorum of the participant devices to vote for it. Configuration rounds advance over time, and a vote is only valid if it was cast in the current round; a vote left over from an older round is stale and must not be counted toward the quorum. There is also a privileged admin override: the admin may authorize an unlock without a quorum. Each time an unlock executes, the system records how many valid current-round votes backed it and whether the admin override was in force at that moment. The concern is that a stale participant or an insufficient set of votes could drive an unauthorized unlock, so every execution must be backed by either a genuine current-round quorum or the admin override. The model tracks the current round, the set of cast votes with their rounds, the admin override flag, and the log of executions.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Every executed unlock was authorized by either a current-round quorum of devices or the admin override.

spec_text:
-------------------------- MODULE W4Od2m7p3t4 --------------------------
(* Warehouse robot fleet allocating docking slots through a compare-and-swap
   register.  To claim a slot a robot performs a CAS that succeeds only if the
   slot's register cell is currently empty, atomically writing its id.  The
   set of usable slots (the capacity) changes at runtime: slots can be brought
   online or taken offline, but a slot can only be taken offline while empty.
   Safety: the same slot is never allocated to two different robots. *)
EXTENDS Naturals

Slots  == {"s1", "s2"}
Robots == {"r1", "r2"}

VARIABLES grants, active

TypeInv ==
    /\ grants \subseteq [slot : Slots, robot : Robots]
    /\ active \subseteq Slots

Init ==
    /\ grants = {}
    /\ active = {"s1"}

Occupied(s) == \E g \in grants : g.slot = s

Activate(s) ==
    /\ s \notin active
    /\ active' = active \union {s}
    /\ UNCHANGED grants

Deactivate(s) ==
    /\ s \in active
    /\ ~Occupied(s)
    /\ active' = active \ {s}
    /\ UNCHANGED grants

CASClaim(r, s) ==
    /\ s \in active
    /\ ~Occupied(s)
    /\ grants' = grants \union {[slot |-> s, robot |-> r]}
    /\ UNCHANGED active

Release(r, s) ==
    /\ [slot |-> s, robot |-> r] \in grants
    /\ grants' = grants \ {[slot |-> s, robot |-> r]}
    /\ UNCHANGED active

Next ==
    \/ \E s \in Slots : Activate(s)
    \/ \E s \in Slots : Deactivate(s)
    \/ \E r \in Robots, s \in Slots : CASClaim(r, s)
    \/ \E r \in Robots, s \in Slots : Release(r, s)

AtMostOneOwnerPerSlot ==
    \A g1, g2 \in grants : (g1.slot = g2.slot) => (g1.robot = g2.robot)

vars == <<grants, active>>
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
=======================================================================

INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT AtMostOneOwnerPerSlot
nl:
In a warehouse robot fleet, docking slots are allocated through a compare-and-swap register, one register cell per slot. To claim a slot, a robot performs a compare-and-swap that succeeds only if the slot's cell is currently empty, in which case it atomically writes its own id into the cell. Because the CAS only fires on an empty cell, two robots cannot both win the same slot. The number of usable slots, the capacity, changes at runtime: slots can be brought online or taken offline as the layout is reconfigured, but a slot may only be taken offline while it is empty. A robot may later release a slot it holds, freeing the cell for reuse. The model tracks the set of active grants and the set of currently online slots.
SAFETY PROPERTY: No slot is ever held by two different robots at the same time.

spec_text:
-------------------------- MODULE W4Od0m6p2t0 --------------------------
(* Hospital operating-room scheduler.  A fixed pool of OR time-blocks (tokens)
   is leased out to scheduler agents.  An agent acquires a block under a lease
   and releases it when done.  An agent may crash silently (it stops acting
   without notice); the lease on a crashed agent's blocks eventually expires,
   returning those blocks to the free pool so nothing is lost.  Safety: the
   total number of time-blocks is conserved -- free plus held always equals
   the fixed total; blocks are never created or destroyed. *)
EXTENDS Naturals

Agents == {"sA", "sB"}
Total  == 2

VARIABLES free, held, status

TypeInv ==
    /\ free \in 0..Total
    /\ held \in [Agents -> 0..Total]
    /\ status \in [Agents -> {"alive", "crashed"}]

Init ==
    /\ free = Total
    /\ held = [a \in Agents |-> 0]
    /\ status = [a \in Agents |-> "alive"]

Acquire(a) ==
    /\ status[a] = "alive"
    /\ free > 0
    /\ free' = free - 1
    /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![a] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED status

Release(a) ==
    /\ status[a] = "alive"
    /\ held[a] > 0
    /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![a] = @ - 1]
    /\ free' = free + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED status

Crash(a) ==
    /\ status[a] = "alive"
    /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![a] = "crashed"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<free, held>>

Recover(a) ==
    /\ status[a] = "crashed"
    /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![a] = "alive"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<free, held>>

LeaseExpire(a) ==
    /\ status[a] = "crashed"
    /\ held[a] > 0
    /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![a] = @ - 1]
    /\ free' = free + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED status

Next ==
    \E a \in Agents :
        \/ Acquire(a)
        \/ Release(a)
        \/ Crash(a)
        \/ Recover(a)
        \/ LeaseExpire(a)

TokenConservation == free + held["sA"] + held["sB"] = Total

vars == <<free, held, status>>
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
=======================================================================
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT TokenConservation
nl:
A hospital operating-room scheduler manages a fixed pool of OR time-blocks that are leased out to scheduler agents. An agent acquires a time-block under a lease, taking it from the free pool, and later releases it back when the block is no longer needed. Agents use lease-based ownership: each held block is covered by a lease that can expire. An agent may crash silently, meaning it simply stops taking actions without announcing anything, potentially while still holding blocks. To ensure nothing is stranded, the lease on a crashed agent's blocks eventually expires and those blocks are returned to the free pool. The essential requirement is that time-blocks are only ever moved between the free pool and the agents, never conjured up or thrown away. The model tracks the free count, the count each agent holds, and each agent's status.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The free blocks plus all blocks held by agents always equal the fixed total, so no time-block is ever created or destroyed.

spec_text:
------------------------- MODULE W4Od10m6p0t2 -------------------------
(* Subway signalling block system.  A track block is the critical resource and
   at most one train may occupy it.  Two independent signalling instances
   (line A and line B) share one common pool of blocks.  A train takes
   lease-based ownership of a block, stamped with an expiry; when the clock
   passes the expiry the lease lapses and the block is vacated.  A train may
   also vacate voluntarily.  Safety: no block is ever occupied by two
   different trains at once. *)
EXTENDS Naturals

Blocks   == {"k1"}
LineA    == {"a1"}
LineB    == {"b1"}
Trains   == LineA \union LineB
MaxClock == 3
Lease    == 2

VARIABLES occ, clock

(* Print-shop job spooler.  A printer is a critical resource that at most one
   job may use at a time.  Jobs are grabbed onto a printer through a
   compare-and-swap register: a start succeeds only if the printer's register
   cell is currently free, atomically binding the job to the printer.  Two
   independent spooler instances share one common pool of jobs feeding the
   printer, so jobs from either instance contend for it.  A job releases the
   printer when it finishes.  Safety: a printer is never bound to two
   different jobs at once. *)

InstanceA  == {"a1"}
InstanceB  == {"b1"}
Jobs       == InstanceA \union InstanceB

VARIABLES spooled, printing

TypeInv ==
    /\ spooled \subseteq Jobs
    /\ printing \subseteq [printer : Printers, job : Jobs]

Init ==
    /\ spooled = {}
    /\ printing = {}

IsPrinting(j) == \E h \in printing : h.job = j
PrinterBusy(pr) == \E h \in printing : h.printer = pr

Spool(j) ==
    /\ j \notin spooled
    /\ ~IsPrinting(j)
    /\ spooled' = spooled \union {j}
    /\ UNCHANGED printing

CASStart(j, pr) ==
    /\ j \in spooled
    /\ ~PrinterBusy(pr)
    /\ printing' = printing \union {[printer |-> pr, job |-> j]}
    /\ spooled' = spooled \ {j}

Finish(h) ==
    /\ h \in printing
    /\ printing' = printing \ {h}
    /\ UNCHANGED spooled

Next ==
    \/ \E j \in Jobs : Spool(j)
    \/ \E j \in Jobs, pr \in Printers : CASStart(j, pr)
    \/ \E h \in printing : Finish(h)

PrinterMutualExclusion ==
    \A h1, h2 \in printing : (h1.printer = h2.printer) => (h1.job = h2.job)

(* Hospital operating-room scheduler.  Finalizing a surgery booking is an
   irreversible action that must happen at most once.  It requires a quorum of
   the review committee to vote in favor.  Vote messages travel over a
   reordering network: they sit in a pending pool and are delivered (tallied)
   in any order.  Once a quorum of tallied votes exists the booking may be
   finalized, but only if it has not already been finalized.  Safety: the
   irreversible finalize happens at most once. *)
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

Committee == {"c1", "c2", "c3"}
Quorum    == 2

VARIABLES pending, votes, commitCount

TypeInv ==
    /\ pending \subseteq [voter : Committee]
    /\ votes \subseteq Committee
    /\ commitCount \in 0..2

Init ==
    /\ pending = {}
    /\ votes = {}
    /\ commitCount = 0

SendVote(d) ==
    /\ d \notin votes
    /\ [voter |-> d] \notin pending
    /\ pending' = pending \union {[voter |-> d]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, commitCount>>

Deliver(m) ==
    /\ m \in pending
    /\ votes' = votes \union {m.voter}
    /\ pending' = pending \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED commitCount

Finalize ==
    /\ Cardinality(votes) >= Quorum
    /\ commitCount = 0
    /\ commitCount' = commitCount + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pending, votes>>

ClearTally ==
    /\ commitCount = 1
    /\ votes' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pending, commitCount>>

Next ==
    \/ \E d \in Committee : SendVote(d)
    \/ \E m \in pending : Deliver(m)
    \/ Finalize
    \/ ClearTally

FinalizeAtMostOnce == commitCount <= 1

   work queue with backpressure: when the queue is full no more units may be
   staged until one is processed out.  Processing a unit emits a release
   request onto a reordering network, where requests sit in an in-flight pool
   and are delivered in any order.  Releasing the flagged unit for transfusion
   is the irreversible action and must happen at most once; once it has
   released, any reordered or duplicate release request is discarded.  Safety:
   the irreversible release happens at most once. *)

Tokens == {"r1", "r2"}
MaxQ   == 3

TypeInv ==
    /\ qlen \in 0..MaxQ
    /\ inflight \subseteq Tokens
    /\ releasedCount \in 0..2

Init ==
    /\ qlen = 0
    /\ inflight = {}
    /\ releasedCount = 0

Enqueue ==
    /\ qlen < MaxQ
    /\ qlen' = qlen + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<inflight, releasedCount>>

Process(t) ==
    /\ qlen > 0
    /\ t \notin inflight
    /\ qlen' = qlen - 1
    /\ inflight' = inflight \union {t}
    /\ UNCHANGED releasedCount

DeliverRelease(t) ==
    /\ t \in inflight
    /\ releasedCount = 0
    /\ releasedCount' = releasedCount + 1
    /\ inflight' = inflight \ {t}
    /\ UNCHANGED qlen

DropRelease(t) ==
    /\ t \in inflight
    /\ releasedCount = 1
    /\ inflight' = inflight \ {t}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<qlen, releasedCount>>

Next ==
    \/ Enqueue
    \/ \E t \in Tokens : Process(t)
    \/ \E t \in Tokens : DeliverRelease(t)
    \/ \E t \in Tokens : DropRelease(t)

    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarseLock, clearedCount>>

    /\ fineLock = NoOne
    /\ coarseLock' = NoOne
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fineLock, clearedCount>>

    /\ washer \in {"alive", "crashed"}

    /\ washer = "alive"

    /\ buf < Cap
    /\ buf' = buf + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED washer

Wash ==
    /\ washer = "alive"
    /\ buf > 0
    /\ buf' = buf - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED washer

Crash ==
    /\ washer = "alive"
    /\ washer' = "crashed"
    /\ UNCHANGED buf

Recover ==
    /\ washer = "crashed"
    /\ washer' = "alive"
    /\ UNCHANGED buf

    \/ Intake
    \/ Wash
    \/ Crash
    \/ Recover
